title: Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied TE Stuart H. Merriam's appeal and sustained Tennessee Valley Presbytery's judgment. It rejected Merriam's procedural claims that the August 10, 2000 called meeting was improperly convened and that TVP was disqualified by prejudice from earlier cases. It found the April 20, 2002 trial properly conducted and, applying BCO 39-3(2), found no clear error in TVP's factual findings. TVP's conviction on three ordination-vow specifications and its indefinite suspension therefore remained in force.
first_summary: The SJC affirmed TE Stuart Merriam's indefinite suspension from Tennessee Valley Presbytery after his 2002 conviction on three ordination-vow specifications, denying his appeal. It rejected his procedural claims that the called meeting was improperly convened and that TVP was prejudiced. Finding no clear error under BCO 39-3(2), it sustained the judgment. Prior SJC Cases 95-10 and 96-7 did not require a different result.
summary: The SJC denied TE Stuart H. Merriam's appeal from Tennessee Valley Presbytery's April 20, 2002 conviction on three ordination-vow specifications and its indefinite suspension. It rejected procedural challenges—that the earlier called meeting was improperly convened and that TVP was prejudiced by prior cases—and found no clear error, applying BCO 39-3(2)'s deference to lower-court factual findings. The SJC sustained TVP's judgment; prior SJC Cases 95-10 and 96-7 had only indirect bearing and did not require retrial.

evidence_notes.dispute: Appeal from TVP's April 20, 2002 conviction of TE Merriam on three ordination-vow specifications and indefinite suspension; issue whether TVP erred procedurally or in judgment. Source lines 35–43, 55–68.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Appeal denied and TVP judgment sustained. Procedural claims of improper meeting call and prejudice were rejected; trial was properly conducted; no clear error under BCO 39-3(2). Source lines 47–102.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Prior SJC Case 95-10 and Judicial Reference 96-7 had only indirect bearing; this was not a retrial. The alleged improperly called meeting was unsupported and, if defective, was cured by the October 10, 2000 stated meeting. Source lines 19–21, 53, 70–82.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None adopted on the merits. Case 95-10 and Case 96-7 are referenced only as background. Source lines 19–21, 53.
